industry.summary: Indian private hospitals are in a growth-and-consolidation phase: listed chains are adding beds at record pace, private equity has built platforms (Blackstone's Quality Care: CARE Hospitals + KIMSHEALTH + Evercare) and is now merging them into listed companies, insurance is a rising share of payment, and tier-2/3 cities are the new battleground. Prices rise with case mix (robotics, transplants, oncology). The counterweights are regulation (price caps, drug mark-ups, government-scheme rates), doctor costs and competition in Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
themes: QCIL (Blackstone/TPG) merged into Aster on 1-Jul-2026, creating the third-largest listed chain by beds (10,898) after Apollo; scale should help procurement (QCIL alone saved ~Rs85 cr in FY26).
ARPP IP +10% in Q1FY27 (pro-forma); robotic surgeries +80%, transplants +19%, joint replacements +39%; CONGO-T specialties (cardiac, oncology, neuro, gastro, ortho, transplants) ~55-59% of revenue.
Walk-in (cash) 53% and corporate/insurance 34% of Q1FY27 revenue; government schemes only 9%: a better payor mix than chains with 17-21% scheme exposure.
International patients +62% in Q1FY27 but only ~4% of revenue: catch-up potential from the GCC, Maldives and Africa, helped by Aster's Gulf brand.
65% of the combined beds are outside metros and tier-1 cities; ~1,300 of QCIL's ~1,700 new beds go to non-metro markets.

On 30-Sep-2026 a Supreme Court bench called mark-ups on medicines sold by corporate hospitals 'carnage', suggested a uniform 16% trade margin and asked the Centre to look at hospitals forcing in-house pharmacy purchases; hospital stocks fell 2-6% that day.
Aster lost doctors in Karnataka in FY26 (single-digit growth in early FY26) and won them back; new competitor hospitals in Bengaluru and Kerala soften growth for 1-2 quarters (Group CFO).

moat: Regional density (Kerala)
Strong
4,642 beds in Kerala after adding KIMSHEALTH (Trivandrum) to Aster Medcity, MIMS Kozhikode/Kannur/Kottakkal; Kerala cluster margin ~25% and occupancy 64% (Q1FY27).
Pricing power and doctor pull in the home market.
Clinical depth (quaternary care)
Advantage
Transplants, robotics (1,300+ robotic cases at Aster in FY26), DBS and liver programmes that can now be shared across 39 hospitals; Aster CMI and Medcity ranked #12 and #28 in India (Newsweek 2026).
Supports case mix and ARPP growth of 7-10% a year.
Scale and procurement
Building
Third-largest listed chain by beds; QCIL saved ~Rs85 cr through central procurement in FY26; merger synergies targeted at Rs150-200 cr.
Real but not yet proven for the merged group (none in Q1FY27).
Payor mix
Advantage
87% cash and corporate/insurance, 9% government schemes, 4% international (Q1FY27).
Less exposed to scheme tariffs than many peers.
Brand
Mixed
Four brands (Aster, CARE, KIMSHEALTH, Evercare) with local strength; the Aster name is shared with a Gulf company the group no longer owns (35% Moopen-owned).
No single national brand; rebranding decisions pending.
Bengaluru and Hyderabad
Weak
Competitive metros: Aster lost doctors in Karnataka in FY26; CARE's Hyderabad assets needed turnarounds; Hyderabad and Sarjapur are new greenfields.
Growth here has to be bought with doctors and capex.
Capital intensity
Neutral
Rs1-1.5 cr a bed; ~Rs4,700 cr of announced expansion over 3-4 years; company ROCE (excl. CWIP, intangibles) 22.9% but return on total capital far lower because of goodwill from acquisitions.
Returns depend on filling new beds.
critiques: Execution risk of integrating two management teams, four brands and 45,000 people while adding 4,179 beds
GAM; analysts on the Q1FY27 call (BNP Paribas, Elara)
Margin guidance (24-25%) depends on synergies not yet seen; Q1FY27 was achieved 'before any synergies'
Valuation already discounts the merger: ~25x forward EBITDA after minorities vs a 36.6x deal multiple for Aster and 25.2x for QCIL
Minorities are large (KIMSHEALTH founder 15-20%, partner-owned hospitals): ~10-13% of EBITDA is not shareholders'
Regulatory risk to pharmacy and consumables margins after the Supreme Court's 30-Sep-2026 remarks
Supply overhang: TPG sold 6.66% in Aug-2026 and still held ~3%; Blackstone (~31%) is a private-equity owner that will sell over time
Street estimates differ widely: FY28E EPS Rs9.7 (ICICI Securities) to Rs18.9 (Motilal Oswal) because of minorities, depreciation and interest assumptions
gaps: QCIL's FY26 consolidated P&L below EBITDA (depreciation, finance cost, other income, tax, minorities, PAT) and its Mar-26 balance sheet are not public; our pro-forma FY26 uses GAM estimates for these (depreciation ~Rs300 cr, finance cost ~Rs200 cr, other income ~Rs20 cr, tax 25%, minorities ~Rs81 cr) and the Sep-25 aggregates from the scheme notice.
QCIL's minority interest is disclosed only for FY24 (Rs1,518 cr book); the share of EBITDA belonging to minorities is not disclosed (we use 11%, between Motilal Oswal's 10% and PL's ~12.5%).
QCIL lease liabilities are not disclosed for Mar-26; we use ~Rs267 cr (Sep-25 net debt incl. leases Rs476 cr less excl. leases Rs209 cr).
No combined ARPOB is disclosed; we use an implied ARPOB on operational beds (hospital revenue / occupied operational bed-days). Occupancy is on census beds, whose count is not disclosed.
Bed-level EBITDA and capex by hospital are not disclosed; the maturity table (Q1FY27) gives revenue and EBITDA shares by bucket only.
Pro-forma Q2FY26 and Q3FY26 revenue/EBITDA are derived from H1 and full-year figures; no combined quarterly KPIs before Q1FY26.
Names and stakes of mutual-fund holders at Jun-2026 were not found; the Sep-2026 pattern (first full post-merger quarter) is outside the as-of window.
Blackstone's exact post-merger stake (30.7% expected less the 'Ancillary Transaction' of up to 2.5%) was not found in a filing dated before 30-Sep-2026.
The accounting effect of pooling (whether FY26 comparatives will be restated) will only be visible in the Q2FY27 accounts.
ICICI Securities' institutional note (Hold, Rs855) could not be read: method and estimates not known.
conflicts: Net debt at Jun-2026: the Q1FY27 deck table labels Aster (511) and the merged entity 1,673, but the Group CFO said combined net debt was Rs1,162 cr with Aster net cash Rs511 cr and QCIL debt Rs1,673 cr; we follow the CFO (the table columns are mislabelled).

Aster occupancy: the Q4FY25 deck shows 65-68% for FY24-FY25 (census-bed basis), while the FY26 deck shows 61% for FY26 and 59%/62% for Q1FY26/Q1FY27; the basis changed and we use the FY26-deck series only.
TPG's August-2026 sale is reported as 6.66% (PTI) and 7.16% (InvestyWise summary); we use 6.66%.
PL's note shows a 'promoter pledge' of Rs71.7 bn; the only pledge disclosures we found (Aug-2026) are by TPG's Centella Mauritius, which is not a promoter.
Margin guidance: the company says 24-25% within two to three years of the merger; HDFC Securities quotes 23-24% for Aster alone and ICICI Securities 23-25% over 3-4 years.
Screener's FY26 net profit (Rs427 cr) is before minorities; the company's Rs388 cr is after. We use Rs388 cr for reported Aster.
